name: What size multifamily project works best for a Glendale infill site?

mainEntity.name: How many units usually make sense on a Glendale ground-up apartment parcel?
mainEntity.text: How many units usually make sense on a Glendale ground-up apartment parcel?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no single ideal unit count for Glendale infill, because project size is driven by what the parcel can physically and financially support. A small lot may only work with a modest number of units if parking and access take up too much of the site. A larger or better-located parcel may support a substantially bigger project with stronger economies of scale. The key is not maximizing units at any cost; it is achieving the best balance between rent potential, construction efficiency, and entitlement risk. A project that is too small may not spread soft costs effectively, while a project that is too large may face zoning, massing, or neighborhood resistance. A good feasibility study will test multiple sizes and compare return on cost, not just total units. That approach often reveals the size where the site finally makes sense.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best project size depends on lot dimensions, zoning, parking, and construction type. In Glendale, a viable infill project may be anywhere from a handful of units on a small lot to a larger podium or mid-rise project on a better-located parcel. The right size is the one that produces enough value after parking and soft costs.
